cases.description: Microsoft's documented example: FALSE in the range evaluates to 0, which is the smallest value
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's worked example for this exact data returns 0, explained on the page as 'Because a value of FALSE evaluates to 0, it is the smallest'. MIN over the same range would return 0.2, because MIN ignores logicals in a reference

cases.description: DIVERGENCE PROBE: all-positive numbers plus a text cell -- Excel counts the text as 0, which becomes the minimum
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's MINA page carries the same self-contradicting pair as MAXA ('text ... evaluate as 0' vs 'text values in the array or reference are ignored'). We assert the text-evaluates-as-0 reading, which AVERAGEA's worked example confirms for the identical wording. Under that reading the answer is 0 (0 < 3); under the 'ignored' reading it would be 3. This case records which reading the engine implements

cases.description: A range of logical TRUEs is a range of 1s
cases.expected_note: Both cells evaluate to 1, so the minimum is 1

cases.description: Truly empty cells are ignored rather than counted as 0
cases.expected_note: Excel documents empty cells as ignored by MINA; if blanks counted as 0 the answer would be 0, so this distinguishes blank handling from text handling

cases.description: A non-numeric string typed directly as an argument is documented as evaluating to 0, which then wins
cases.expected_note: Verbatim from Microsoft's MINA page: 'Arguments that contain text or FALSE evaluate as 0 (zero)'. Under that rule the literal "abc" becomes 0, which is smaller than 5. MIN's page carries the opposite rule, so this case checks the A-variant rule is applied

cases.description: An error value passed as an argument propagates instead of being coerced
cases.expected_note: Error values are not coerced by MINA; NA() produces #N/A and that error is the result
